correctness.rationale: Under the stated independent Poisson model the total means depend only on the effort-weighted index m; because the full interval is attained, no randomized or multiseason allocation is needed to realize an optimum. This proves uniqueness of the effective index, not of dates or allocation histories. Strict log concavity follows by differentiating both positive factors. The derivative at m=0 is strictly positive since z/(exp(Bz)−1) decreases, and an endpoint is optimal exactly when the derivative there is nonnegative. At m=1 write x=α(1+u), y=β(1−u). If y≤x the derivative is negative for every finite B, even at equality because β>α. If y>x the log derivative of (exp(By)−1)/(exp(Bx)−1) is positive by monotonicity of z/(1−exp(−Bz)), and the ratio increases from y/x<β/α to infinity. This yields one boundary budget including equality at onset. At an interior solution, y(m)>x(m); the stationarity log ratio increases in B there and decreases in m, proving strict movement until saturation. Expanding stationarity uniformly at small B gives 0=−2um/(1−u²m²)+B(β−α)/2+O(B²), so the stated small-B coefficient follows. For the permanent-interior regimes including equality, both rates are bounded away from zero and stationarity gives B(y−x)=log(β/α)+O(exp(−cB)), yielding the asserted approach. The example polynomial changes sign from 3.9 to 4 and is strictly increasing for z>3 after decreasing on (1,3); independent numerical bisections agree with the recorded B_c and m₁.
residual_risks: The equivalence by effective index is only for the specified objective and effort model. Several times can have the same index; independence, known presence and attainability of all indices matter.

originality.rationale: The independent all-detected product, concave log objective, and temporal allocation framing have closely related indexed instances and general antecedents. The strongest available analogous statements use different normalized hazard frontiers or objectives. No inspected comparison yields the specific affine-frontier classification with an iff finite saturation test and strict monotonicity of the optimizer up to it. Credit is limited to that distinction and its quantitative consequences, not the Poisson reduction or KKT stationarity alone.
residual_risks: Full texts of Rounds et al. and Moore–McCarthy were not accessible; their inspected public material does not settle whole-paper coverage.
Relative publication order of same-date records is unresolved and is not presumed. A differently named reliability/comparative-statics theorem could be equivalent; search is bounded.

value.rationale: The meaningful ecological decision is whether increasing a prescribed effort can eventually remove the need for a compromise season. The sharp endpoint-rate comparison answers that with an equality case that remains strictly interior at every finite budget, a unique threshold where it exists, and quantitative approach otherwise. The result adds a testable model benchmark beyond a generic optimizer existence or stationarity result; it is not empirical calibration or a claim that seasonal replication is generally useless.
residual_risks: Different objectives, incomplete seasonal access, occupancy uncertainty, correlated counts and visit costs can all change the recommended design.
